transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Lately I’ve been overwhelmed by guilt about letting everyone down at home and at work, even when people tell me it’s not that bad. It just feels like no matter what I do, I'm failing the people who depend on me.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this overwhelmed and guilty in the past, perhaps months or years ago, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

No, this isn't the first time. I've actually had these cycles of feeling highly energized for a few weeks and then sinking into these long, drained stretches on and off for at least a few years. They've just become much more noticeable and harder to manage over the past year with the growing pressures at home and work.

During those periods when you felt highly energized, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual, felt unusually talkative, or engaged in risky behaviors that were out of character for you?

Yes, during those weeks I only slept about four hours a night but woke up feeling completely wired. I was also talking so fast and jumping between ideas that coworkers joked I wouldn't let anyone get a word in. I didn't do anything dangerous, but I did impulsively overcommit to way too many projects because I felt like I could handle anything.

During those highly energized periods, did you ever feel like you were losing touch with reality, such as hearing voices, seeing things that weren't there, or feeling like you had special powers or hidden knowledge?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. While I felt extremely confident, capable, and full of ideas during those high-energy periods, I have never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or felt like I had supernatural powers or hidden knowledge.
During those low, drained periods you described, have you ever felt that high-energy, 'wired' feeling at the same time as the deep sadness or guilt?

No, I don't think I've ever felt both of those at the same time. For me, they have always been distinct, separate phases—first I'll have that high-energy period, and then it's followed by the low, drained slump.
During these low, drained periods, have you felt so hopeless or physically slowed down that you were unable to function at work or perform basic daily tasks?

Yes, my body feels like it's moving through molasses—I catch myself staring at my computer unable to type, and even loading the dishwasher takes everything I've got. It has absolutely impacted my ability to function, and I've been missing deadlines and forgetting meetings to the point that my team has had to pick up my slack. My coworkers have even commented on how slowly I walk down the hallways lately.
During these recent low periods, have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or have you felt so overwhelmed that you considered harming yourself?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself or felt like life isn't worth living. Even though I feel incredibly overwhelmed, exhausted, and guilty right now, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
